issues.description: The required 'Open Questions' section is entirely missing from the proposal.
issues.suggested_fix: Add an 'Open Questions' section at the end of the document to address unresolved, contradicted, or low-confidence items.

issues.description: The proposal states a strict $300,000 budget cap as a fact, ignoring the contradiction in the Client Matrix where Sarah claims the range is $250k to $400k while Rita insists on a $300k cap.
issues.suggested_fix: Remove the definitive $300,000 cap commitment. Present a proposed cost or range, and move the budget cap discrepancy to the 'Open Questions' section for client alignment.

issues.description: The proposal presents the portable logic layer as the 'definitive strategy', ignoring the fundamental contradiction between Marcus (who wants a platform replacement) and Sarah/Rita (who want a short-term workflow fix).
issues.suggested_fix: Frame the portable architecture as a proposed compromise rather than a 'definitive strategy', and add the platform replacement vs. short-term fix debate to the 'Open Questions' section.

issues.description: The proposal commits to a Q3 (September 30) pilot deployment as a definitive target, ignoring Marcus's explicit disagreement regarding the feasibility of a Q3 deadline.
issues.suggested_fix: Remove the hard commitment to the Q3 deadline. Frame it as an aggressive target to be evaluated during Phase 1, and add the timeline feasibility to the 'Open Questions' section.

risks: By stating contradicted items (budget, timeline, and technical strategy) as agreed-upon facts, the proposal risks alienating key stakeholders (like Marcus) who hold opposing views, potentially derailing the pitch.
The complete omission of the 'Open Questions' section prevents the consulting team from facilitating necessary alignment discussions among the client's divided leadership team.
